**Styregruppen for AFDK** (the Steering Committee for the Atrial Fibrillation in Denmark database) is the professional governing body responsible for overseeing the national clinical quality database [[atrieflimren-i-danmark|Atrieflimren i Danmark]] [^src2]. Operating under the [[regionernes-kliniske-kvalitetsudviklingsprogram|Regionernes Kliniske Kvalitetsudviklingsprogram]] (RKKP) [^src8], the committee is tasked with deciding on the retention of clinical indicators, establishing quality standards, and issuing strategic recommendations to improve cardiovascular care across Danish regions and health clusters [^src1].

The committee's work directly shapes national clinical guidelines and performance targets. For instance, it has established a 90% target fulfillment rate for anticoagulation treatment as good clinical practice [^src2]. For [[indikator-5|Indikator 5]], which tracks the incidence of ischemic stroke among prevalent atrial fibrillation patients, the committee set a strict standard of ≤ 0.8 per 100 risk years based on current data and literature [^src5]. The committee also governs [[indikator-3|Indikator 3]] (TSH measurement at diagnosis) [^src9] and issues recommendations for [[indikator-4b|Indikator 4b]], advocating for greater focus on renal function monitoring for patients discharged on DOAC medications [^src7]. Furthermore, the committee has conducted validation work on [[indikator-2|Indikator 2]], revealing significant underreporting of echocardiography procedures to the National Patient Register [^src3].

Beyond setting standards, the committee addresses systemic data and operational challenges. It has identified issues with varying codes for [[thyreoideastimulerende-hormon-tsh|thyreoideastimulerende hormon (TSH)]] measurements in [[labka|LABKA]] and is working to ensure all relevant codes are captured and transferred to RKKP [^src6]. Looking ahead, the committee is considering age-standardizing all outcome indicators to account for demographic shifts and an expected increase in intracranial hemorrhages [^src8]. To improve patient-facing initiatives, the committee collaborates directly with [[afdk-patientrepraesentanter|Patientrepræsentanterne i AFDK]] to operationalize structured patient education, addressing the systemic failure to meet the national 50% standard for Indicator 8 [^src1].

The committee is chaired by [[axel-brandes|Axel Brandes]] [^src10] and comprises a multidisciplinary group of leading physicians, cardiologists, nurses, general practitioners, epidemiologists, data managers, and patient representatives, including [[inge-molgaard|Inge Mølgaard]] and [[robert-bedsted|Robert Bedsted]] [^src10]. Through its ongoing evaluations and audits, the committee ensures that the AFDK database remains a robust tool for population-based quality measurement and cross-sectoral healthcare improvement [^src2].
